exercises.title: Bài 1 · What are international relations?
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
International relations is the study of how states and other actors behave in the world. The main actors are sovereign states, which have the highest authority inside their borders. However, non-state actors, such as multinational corporations and international organizations, are becoming more important every year.

Scholars use different theories to explain world politics. Realists believe that states act to protect their national interest and that power, especially hard power such as military strength, is decisive. Liberals say that cooperation is possible, because states are connected by trade and shared institutions. This interdependence makes war more expensive.

In practice, countries use both hard power and soft power, which is the ability to attract others through culture and values. A government may build alliances, sign bilateral and multilateral agreements, and try to keep a balance of power in its region.

content.q: Sovereign states have the highest authority inside their borders.
content.why: Đoạn 1: quốc gia có chủ quyền có thẩm quyền cao nhất trong biên giới.

content.q: Non-state actors are becoming less important.
content.why: Đoạn 1: chủ thể phi nhà nước ngày càng **quan trọng hơn**.

content.q: Realists believe that cooperation is the most important factor.
content.why: Đoạn 2: người theo chủ nghĩa hiện thực nhấn mạnh quyền lực và lợi ích quốc gia.

content.q: Soft power is the ability to attract others through culture and values.
Which is an example of a non-state actor?
content.why: Đoạn 1: tập đoàn đa quốc gia là chủ thể phi nhà nước.

content.q: What do liberals say?
content.why: Đoạn 2: phái tự do tin vào hợp tác nhờ thương mại và thể chế chung.
opts: Cooperation is possible because states are connected by trade

content.q: What does interdependence do?
content.why: Đoạn 2: phụ thuộc lẫn nhau khiến chiến tranh tốn kém hơn.

content.q: What may a government do to keep a balance of power?
content.why: Đoạn 3: lập liên minh, ký thỏa thuận để giữ cân bằng quyền lực.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Inside an embassy
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
An embassy is the main diplomatic office of one country in another. It is led by an ambassador, who is appointed by the head of state and who presents credentials to the host country. The embassy is staffed by diplomats, attachés and local employees.

Diplomats have several tasks. They represent their government, report on political and economic developments, and negotiate with officials of the host country. A consulate, which is run by a consul, helps citizens abroad, for example by issuing passports and giving assistance in emergencies. Visas are also processed there.

Diplomats are protected by diplomatic immunity, so they cannot be arrested in the host country. This protection is given so that they can work freely. However, if a diplomat behaves badly, he or she can be declared persona non grata and expelled. Important events, such as summits and state visits, are organised according to strict protocol.

content.q: An embassy is led by an ambassador.
content.why: Đoạn 1: đại sứ đứng đầu đại sứ quán.

content.q: Diplomats can be arrested in the host country at any time.
content.why: Đoạn 3: nhờ quyền miễn trừ ngoại giao, họ không thể bị bắt.

content.q: A consulate helps citizens abroad.
content.why: Đoạn 2: lãnh sự quán hỗ trợ công dân, cấp hộ chiếu, hỗ trợ khẩn cấp.

content.q: A diplomat who behaves badly can never be expelled.
content.why: Đoạn 3: có thể bị tuyên bố persona non grata và bị trục xuất.

content.q: Who appoints an ambassador?
content.why: Đoạn 1: đại sứ do nguyên thủ quốc gia bổ nhiệm.

content.q: What is one task of diplomats?
content.why: Đoạn 2: đại diện, báo cáo tình hình và đàm phán.
opts: Reporting on political and economic developments

content.q: What may happen to a diplomat who behaves badly?
content.why: Đoạn 3: có thể bị trục xuất.
opts: He or she is made consul
He or she can be expelled
He or she is given a visa

content.q: How are summits and state visits organised?
content.why: Đoạn 3: theo nghi lễ ngoại giao nghiêm ngặt.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · The United Nations system
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
The United Nations was created in 1945 to maintain international peace and security. Today almost every country is a member state. The General Assembly is the largest body: every member has one vote, and its resolutions are important political statements, although they are usually less binding than those of the Security Council.

The Security Council has fifteen members. Five of them, the permanent members, hold a veto, so one of them can stop a resolution. Decisions on peacekeeping are therefore harder to reach than ordinary votes. The Secretary-General leads the Secretariat, which runs the day-to-day work from the headquarters in New York.

Other organizations are more specialized. The World Trade Organization sets rules for trade, while the IMF and the World Bank support financial stability and development. NGOs often provide humanitarian aid faster and more flexibly than governments.

content.q: The United Nations was created in 1945.
content.why: Đoạn 1: LHQ được thành lập năm 1945.

content.q: In the General Assembly, the permanent members have more votes.
content.why: Đoạn 1: mỗi thành viên có **một** phiếu.

content.q: A permanent member of the Security Council can stop a resolution with a veto.
content.why: Đoạn 2: thành viên thường trực có quyền phủ quyết.

content.q: The headquarters of the Secretariat is in Geneva.
content.why: Đoạn 2: trụ sở ở New York.

content.q: How do General Assembly resolutions compare with Security Council resolutions?
content.why: Đoạn 1: thường ít ràng buộc hơn.

content.q: How many members does the Security Council have?
content.why: Đoạn 2: 15 thành viên, trong đó 5 thường trực.

content.q: What does the Secretariat do?
content.why: Đoạn 2: ban thư ký điều hành công việc hằng ngày.

content.q: What is the role of the WTO?
content.why: Đoạn 3: WTO đặt ra quy tắc thương mại.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How a treaty is made
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A treaty is a binding agreement between states. The process usually starts with negotiation. Delegations must prepare an agenda, and they have to agree on the text article by article. Both sides should make concessions, because a win-win outcome is more likely to last. If talks reach a deadlock, a mediator may help.

After the negotiation, the text is signed by the representatives of the states, who are then called signatories. Signature alone does not bind a state. The treaty usually has to be ratified by the parliament or another national body. A state that was not involved at the beginning can accede later. Some states make a reservation to exclude a provision.

The treaty enters into force when the required number of states have ratified it. From then on, the parties must act in good faith, and they mustn't violate its rules. Disputes may be brought before the International Court of Justice.

content.q: Delegations have to agree on the text article by article.
content.why: Đoạn 1: thống nhất văn bản từng điều một.

content.q: Signature alone always makes a treaty binding.
content.why: Đoạn 2: chữ ký không đủ; thường cần phê chuẩn.

content.q: A state that did not take part in the negotiation can accede later.
content.why: Đoạn 2: quốc gia không tham gia ban đầu có thể gia nhập sau.

content.q: Parties to a treaty are free to violate its rules.
content.why: Đoạn 3: các bên **không được** vi phạm (mustn't violate).

content.q: Why should both sides make concessions?
content.why: Đoạn 1: kết quả đôi bên cùng có lợi bền vững hơn.
opts: A win-win outcome is more likely to last
It removes the need for ratification

content.q: Who may help if talks reach a deadlock?
content.why: Đoạn 1: hòa giải viên có thể giúp.

content.q: What do some states do with a reservation?
content.why: Đoạn 2: bảo lưu để loại trừ một điều khoản.

content.q: When does a treaty enter into force?
content.why: Đoạn 3: khi đủ số quốc gia phê chuẩn.
opts: When the required number of states have ratified it
As soon as it is signed

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Preventing a crisis
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Imagine that two neighbouring states are in a serious crisis over a border area. Tension is rising, and both armies are moving troops. If the situation escalates, a military conflict may begin, and thousands of civilians will become refugees.

What can the international community do? If diplomats act quickly, they can organise peace talks. The United Nations may send peacekeepers if the parties accept a ceasefire. Other states can use sanctions or an embargo to put pressure on the aggressor, although these measures do not always work. If the great powers cooperated more closely, many crises would be easier to solve.

In the long term, deterrence, disarmament and non-proliferation reduce the risk of war. Intelligence services also help governments understand threats early. But experts agree that stability depends mainly on trust: if states trusted each other more, they would spend less on weapons.

content.q: If a crisis escalates, a military conflict may begin.
content.why: Đoạn 1: nếu leo thang, xung đột quân sự có thể bắt đầu.

content.q: Sanctions always succeed in stopping aggression.
content.why: Đoạn 2: các biện pháp này không phải lúc nào cũng hiệu quả.

content.q: The UN may send peacekeepers if the parties accept a ceasefire.
content.why: Đoạn 2: LHQ có thể cử lực lượng gìn giữ hòa bình.

content.q: Experts say that stability depends mainly on weapons.
content.why: Đoạn 3: ổn định phụ thuộc chủ yếu vào **niềm tin**.

content.q: What will happen to civilians if the situation escalates?
content.why: Đoạn 1: hàng nghìn dân thường sẽ thành người tị nạn.

content.q: What can diplomats organise if they act quickly?
What would happen if the great powers cooperated more closely?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nhiều cuộc khủng hoảng sẽ dễ giải quyết hơn.
opts: Many crises would be easier to solve

content.q: What does stability depend on, according to experts?
content.why: Đoạn 3: niềm tin giữa các quốc gia.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Global problems, shared solutions
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
In the past few decades, the world has faced problems that no country can solve alone. Climate change is the clearest example. Global emissions have risen steadily since the industrial revolution, and extreme weather has caused heavy losses in many regions. Last year, leaders met at a climate summit and agreed to set stronger targets for renewable energy and carbon neutrality.

Other challenges are linked to global inequality. The pandemic disrupted supply chains and showed how weak health systems can be. Poverty has fallen in many countries since 2000, but food security and water scarcity remain serious. Rich countries have provided development aid, and organizations have worked on capacity building in poorer states.

Foreign direct investment and free trade have created jobs, but they have also raised questions about human rights and the environment. As a result, many governments have started to discuss new rules for global governance.

content.q: Global emissions have risen steadily since the industrial revolution.
content.why: Đoạn 1: khí thải tăng đều từ cách mạng công nghiệp.

content.q: Leaders agreed to set weaker targets at the climate summit.
content.why: Đoạn 1: họ đồng ý đặt mục tiêu **mạnh hơn**.

content.q: The pandemic disrupted supply chains.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đại dịch làm gián đoạn chuỗi cung ứng.

content.q: Poverty has increased in all countries since 2000.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nghèo đói đã giảm ở nhiều nước từ năm 2000.

content.q: What did leaders agree to do at the climate summit?
content.why: Đoạn 1: đặt mục tiêu mạnh hơn về năng lượng tái tạo và trung hòa carbon.
opts: Set stronger targets for renewable energy and carbon neutrality

content.q: What did the pandemic show?
content.why: Đoạn 2: hệ thống y tế có thể yếu kém đến mức nào.
opts: How weak health systems can be

content.q: What have rich countries provided?
What questions have FDI and free trade raised?
content.why: Đoạn 3: các câu hỏi về nhân quyền và môi trường.
opts: Questions about human rights and the environment
